descriptive_title: Grade 1 Mathematics: Demonstrations — Geometric Shapes, Position, and Movement (E1.1-E1.5)
subject: Mathematics

curriculum_expectations.E1.1: sort three-dimensional objects and two-dimensional shapes according to one attribute at a time, and identify the sorting rule being used
curriculum_expectations.E1.2: construct three-dimensional objects, and identify two-dimensional shapes contained within structures and objects
curriculum_expectations.E1.3: construct and describe two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional objects that have matching halves
curriculum_expectations.E1.4: describe the relative locations of objects or people, using positional language
curriculum_expectations.E1.5: give and follow directions for moving from one location to another

unit_overview: A 5-day Grade 1 unit on spatial sense (E1.1-E1.5) framed around 'Map It, Move It!' — Trekker Tig the Tiger Cub and Compass Coco the Cat. Day 1 sorts 2D and 3D shapes by attribute. Day 2 builds 3D structures and finds 2D shapes inside. Day 3 makes shapes with matching halves (symmetry). Day 4 describes relative locations with position words. Day 5 gives and follows directions in a Treasure Trail Capstone. Each lesson includes an expanded_walkthrough.
unit_learning_goal: Children will sort shapes by attribute, build 3D structures, identify 2D shapes within them, make shapes with matching halves, describe locations, and give/follow directions.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We sort shapes by ONE attribute. Same shapes can be sorted in DIFFERENT ways.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can sort shapes by one rule and name the rule.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Tig sorts a shape pile by attribute; children sort and name their rule.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We can BUILD 3D structures. Inside every structure are 2D SHAPES.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can build a 3D structure and find 2D shapes inside it.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children build with paper blocks; identify 2D shapes on the faces.

lesson_arc.big_idea: A shape with MATCHING HALVES has a line of SYMMETRY. Each half is a MIRROR of the other.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can make shapes with matching halves.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Coco folds shapes; children identify and create matching-halves shapes.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We describe LOCATION with position words: above, below, beside, between, in front, behind.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can describe where something is using position words.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Tig hides treasures; children describe locations on a map.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We can GIVE and FOLLOW directions to move from one place to another.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can give and follow directions to move.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children write directions, follow a partner's directions, and find the treasure.

recurring_characters.name: Trekker Tig the Tiger Cub
recurring_characters.role: Lead character. A young tiger cub explorer who loves hiking trails and finding treasures. Anchors all 5 lessons.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A young tiger cub with stripes wearing a small explorer's hat and backpack. Carries a walking stick. Bright eyes, curious expression.

recurring_characters.name: Compass Coco the Cat
recurring_characters.role: Tig's partner. The 'directions' character — holds a compass and gives bearings. Cameo Lessons 3-5.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A young cat with a small compass on a chain around its neck and a tiny map under one paw. Calm, focused expression.

threaded_vocabulary.child_friendly_definition: A way to describe a shape — colour, shape, size, etc.
How we decide what goes in each group.
A 3D thing we built — like a tower or a hut.
Two equal parts of a whole.
Two halves that are the SAME — mirror twins.
An instruction to move — like 'forward 3 steps'.

pedagogical_notes: Grade 1 spatial work is concrete — children handle real shapes and build real structures.
Sorting precedes building — children must categorize shapes confidently before construction.
Symmetry (matching halves) introduced via folding — fold-and-cut, fold-and-look.
Position language must be precise — 'beside' is different from 'between'.
Direction-giving uses a turtle-style language: 'forward 3, turn right, forward 2'.
canadian_context_notes: Use Canadian places for treasure maps: cabins, lakes, maple trees, snow-covered hills.
Reference Canadian symbols: maple leaf (with line of symmetry), flag.
Hockey rink layout (rectangles, circles) for shape inside structure.
Compass directions familiar to Canadian students from outdoor education.
